summary: 37 prop meshes. Round 2 (12 Nov 2026): 24 of them now carry a unique bake from a high-detail source (BC / N / ORM, E where lit; true metal in ORM.B; subsurface and translucent slot kinds; non-overlapping UV0): the four light sources, candle alias, barrel, chest (+ new opened-lid variant SM_Chest_Small_Open_PR), two crates, long and round table, bench, stool, chair, bed (cloth-simulated blanket and pillow), four pots, two sacks (cloth simulation), skull and bones scatter. 13 props are still round-1 tiling sets with vertex-colour weathering (gravestones, fireplace, basket, pie, potion flask, counter, post, cabinet, pillar, rubble, bottle shelf). Two decal texture sets (blood splat, burn hole) are in Props/Decals. Nothing is claimed photoreal where known_weaknesses lists faults, which is every asset.
review: Round 2: Props/review/r5 and r6, per baked prop: sun and sky at the game camera (45 degrees down from 6 m), a 1 m close-up, a warm dim interior light (plus the opened chest and a skull side view), 96 samples on the GPU, looked at and criticised two to five rounds each (counts in known_weaknesses). Round 1 props: review/r1-r4. The decals were judged on a flat lit preview (Props/Decals/preview.png), not in Cycles.

all_assets.material_exception: shared tiling scan sets with a vertex-colour weathering layer (MI_Prop_* / MI_Struct_*), not private bakes and not yet rows of ART_STANDARD.md section 2. Edge wear, stains and soot are per-vertex. A unique bake per prop is the next step where the weaknesses say so.

SM_Prop_Torch_Wall_01.known_weaknesses: Round 2, four review rounds (r5-r6). Last look still faults: the rag head reads as stiff overlapping bands rather than soft wound cloth (the game mesh has two wound strips, the other strips, tails and frayed threads are baked), dark and matte now but without loose hanging ends in silhouette; pitch drips on the stave are normal-map only; the smoke plate is a plain rectangle of sheet whose soot fades in a soft procedural edge; the stave grain is a scan recoloured, a little uniform along its length. No flame mesh (engine effect).
SM_Prop_Torch_Wall_01.dresses: wall torch, 0.16 x 0.36 x 0.95 m: forged back plate on two square-headed spikes, a sheet-iron smoke plate curled at the top and sooted above the flame, a twisted square bracket arm and stay with two riveted bands gripping a cleft ash stave at 19 degrees, the head a wad of pitch-soaked hessian wound in strips with torn tails, frayed charred fibres, wire binding and runs of pitch down the stave (baked)

emissive+.note: point light 10 cm above the socket; T_Prop_Torch_Wall_01_E is the ember mask of the charred rag end (emissive = E * 40 nits * flicker when lit, 0 when unlit); the flame itself is an engine effect

SM_Prop_Brazier_Standing_01.known_weaknesses: Round 2, three review rounds (r5-r6). Last look still faults: charcoal lumps are faceted blobs that read slightly like dark rock in full sun (no long split-wood charcoal shapes); straps are even in width; rivets on the hoops are baked, not geometry; the ash pan is a plain dish. Ember glow (E) reads well in the dark.
SM_Prop_Brazier_Standing_01.dresses: standing fire basket, 0.72 x 0.70 x 0.99 m: three twisted square forged legs with beaten feet, collar and stretcher ring, a basket of ten flaring straps riveted to three hoops over an ash pan, a heaped bed of charcoal with ash on the tops and live embers in the gaps (emissive mask)

emissive+.note: point light 15 cm above the socket, soft radius 12 cm, flicker 10-20 percent; T_Prop_Brazier_Standing_01_E is the ember bed mask (emissive = E * 120 nits, slow pulse 0.7-1.0; 0 when unlit); a dim red fill light inside the basket is still worth adding

SM_Prop_Candle_Holder_01.known_weaknesses: Round 2, three review rounds. Last look faults little: the pricket stick is a clean lathe (hammer texture only in the normal), the puddle in the pan is thin, the wick is a plain bent tube. Wax needs the subsurface slot honoured in engine or it reads as chalk.

emissive+.note: point light 2 cm above the wick, soft radius 1 cm, slow flicker 5-10 percent; slot MI_Prop_Candle_Holder_01_Wax is kind subsurface (the wax near the flame glows by scattering; no emissive mask)

SM_Prop_Lantern_Hanging_01.known_weaknesses: Round 2, four review rounds (r5-r6). Last look still faults: the pyramid cap is plain flat sheet (vents and rivets are baked only, no seam or lapped edge), frame bars are clean square section, the horn panes are flat with a cloudy amber pattern that is a little even from pane to pane, chain links are plain ovals; inside there is only a candle stub (no pricket). Lit state depends on the integrator honouring the translucent slot and E.
SM_Prop_Lantern_Hanging_01.dresses: hanging lantern, 0.19 x 0.19 x 0.78 m with its chain: riveted iron tray and pierced pyramid cap, four corner bars, four scraped-horn panes each with a glazing bar, door hinges and hasp (baked), a candle stub inside, seven links of chain to a ceiling hook and plate

fit+.panes: slot MI_Prop_Lantern_Hanging_01_Horn is kind translucent (thin, two-sided, diffusing amber horn: transmission colour = BC, about 60 percent of light carried through); T_Prop_Lantern_Hanging_01_E holds the glow of the panes around the candle (emissive = E * 60 nits when lit, 0 unlit)

emissive+.note: point light at the socket with shadow casting off for the lantern mesh itself; pane glow from E as in fit.panes

SM_Barrel_Oak_PR.known_weaknesses: Round 2 unique bake, three review rounds (r6). Last look still faults: the joints between staves are drawn as even dark lines (AO dirt) rather than varying gaps; rust runs under the hoops are faint; the hoops are flat strap with baked rivets at the lap only; head boards have no chalk or brand marks; the chime is not undercut. Broken states not built.
SM_Barrel_Oak_PR.dresses: coopered oak barrel, 0.84 m at the bilge, 1.0 m: twenty separate staves of uneven width with gaps, five-board heads sawn round and set in the croze, four driven hoops a touch out of level with riveted laps (baked), a bung; true-metal hoops with rust, handling grease and a damp tide mark at the foot

SM_Crate_Large_PR.known_weaknesses: Round 2 unique bake, two review rounds (r6). Last look still faults: boards are straight-sawn with only slight warp, no split or missing slat, nail heads are baked and small, no stencil or brand, scratch marks are a little even over all faces. Low triangle count (312): slats are single boxes.
SM_Crate_Large_PR.dresses: slatted packing crate 0.97 x 0.67 x 0.58 m: four corner posts inside, three slats a side with open gaps onto a real interior with bottom boards, four lid boards under two nailed battens; weathered grey-brown softwood, damp at the foot

SM_Crate_Small_PR.known_weaknesses: As SM_Crate_Large_PR (same generator, its own bake and board layout).
SM_Crate_Small_PR.dresses: slatted packing crate 0.74 x 0.55 x 0.47 m, built as SM_Crate_Large_PR with three lid boards

SM_Jar_Storage_PR.known_weaknesses: Round 2 unique bake, two review rounds (r6). Last look still faults: glaze runs are thin dark streaks, not thick beaded drips; chips at rim and foot are small; glaze colour is even around the body apart from throwing rings; no clear-coat layer (single specular lobe), the inside is glazed like the outside and falls to black.
SM_Jar_Storage_PR.dresses: wheel-thrown storage jar, 0.51 x 0.74 m, rolled rim, brown lead glaze with throwing rings, runs, crazing and pinholes over a bare biscuit foot with a wavy glaze line; thrown out of true, hollow to a real inner wall

SM_Jar_Jug_PR.known_weaknesses: As SM_Jar_Storage_PR; the strap handles are plain flattened tubes thumbed on without finger marks.
SM_Jar_Jug_PR.dresses: two-handled crock, 0.55 x 0.58 m, blue-grey glaze, two pulled strap handles; otherwise as the storage jar

SM_Jar_Vase_PR.known_weaknesses: As SM_Jar_Storage_PR; the ox-red glaze is saturated and even.
SM_Jar_Vase_PR.dresses: narrow-necked bottle vase, 0.25 x 0.68 m, ox-red glaze; otherwise as the storage jar

SM_Jar_Bowl_PR.known_weaknesses: As SM_Jar_Storage_PR; cream glaze inside with a dull pooled centre; empty (sprite frames 2-3 show a yellow content).
SM_Jar_Bowl_PR.dresses: footed dish, 0.42 x 0.17 m, brown outside, cream glaze inside, turned foot ring

SM_Sack_Grain_PR.known_weaknesses: Round 2 unique bake from a cloth simulation (sewn pouch inflated by pressure and dropped on the floor), four review rounds (r6). Last look still faults: the cloth is clean (few stains, no patch or stencil), folds are the soft dimples of an inflated cushion rather than the sag of loose grain, the rolled hem, twine stitches and side seams are baked into the normal map only, so the mouth has no silhouette detail. Colour variants of round 1 (olive, madder) are now a BC tint for the integrator.
SM_Sack_Grain_PR.dresses: full grain sack lying on its side, 0.97 x 0.69 x 0.26 m: jute sackcloth (hessian scan), simulated bulge with pinched corner ears, rolled and whip-stitched mouth at +X with a loose tail of twine, sewn side seams (baked)

SM_FeedSack_Jute_PR.known_weaknesses: Round 2 unique bake from a cloth simulation (bag pinned at the tie, inflated, settled on the floor), three review rounds (r6). Last look still faults: clean cloth with few stains; the ruff above the tie is a procedural gathered form, stiffer than the simulated body; the twine tie is one ring on the game mesh (five turns baked); no side seam in silhouette.
SM_FeedSack_Jute_PR.dresses: feed sack stood on end, 0.74 x 0.56 x 0.77 m: jute sackcloth, weight settled to the bottom with simulated pleats running up to a gathered neck whipped with twine, a ruff of loose cloth above the tie flopping to one side

SM_Table_Oak_Long_PR.known_weaknesses: Round 2 unique bake, two review rounds (r6). Last look still faults: about 700 px/m on a 2.65 m table, so the top is soft at 1 m; knife scores and mug rings are present but faint, spills read as blotches; board ends carry long-grain texture (no end grain); pegs are baked discs; legs and rails are straight square stock. Only 252 triangles.
SM_Table_Oak_Long_PR.dresses: oak table 2.65 x 1.5 x 0.905 m: six-board top with uneven ends and slight steps between boards, four square tapered legs, rails and foot rails pegged into the legs (pegs baked), a long stretcher; dark handled oak with scores, rings and greasy polish on the top

SM_Table_Oak_Round_PR.known_weaknesses: As SM_Table_Oak_Long_PR; the round outline is sawn per board in ten segments, a little polygonal at 1 m.
SM_Table_Oak_Round_PR.dresses: round oak table, 1.6 m across, 0.8 m: seven boards sawn to the round on two battens, four tapered legs, crossed stretchers

SM_Chair_Oak_PR.known_weaknesses: Round 2 unique bake, two review rounds. Last look faults little at gameplay distance; at 1 m: members are straight square stock except the raked back legs, joints show no shoulders, pegs are baked, seat boards are flat (no saddle or wear hollow).
SM_Chair_Oak_PR.dresses: joined oak side chair, 0.52 x 0.56 x 1.0 m: raked back legs with a kicked foot, three-board seat, seat rails and stretchers, shaped crest rail and a slat, pegged (baked)

SM_Bench_Oak_PR.known_weaknesses: Round 2 unique bake, two review rounds. Last look still faults: one clean thick board with slight warp; boot notches are a simple splayed V; texture soft at 1 m (2.3 m bench in one 2048 set); no end grain.
SM_Bench_Oak_PR.dresses: plank bench 2.3 x 0.3 x 0.46 m: one thick board on two slab ends with boot notches, through tenons standing proud of the seat, a pegged stretcher

SM_Stool_Oak_PR.known_weaknesses: Round 2 unique bake, three review rounds (radial seat grain fixed). Last look still faults: legs meet the seat without visible wedged tenons on top; the seat rim carries stretched grain; turned legs are simple tapers.
SM_Stool_Oak_PR.dresses: three-legged stool, 0.36 m dished plank seat, 0.45 m, splayed shaved legs

SM_Bed_Oak_PR.known_weaknesses: Round 2 unique bake with cloth simulation (blanket and pillow; cached in _build/bake/cache), five review rounds (r6). Last look still faults: the blanket lies too flat on top (the 7 percent slack gave only shallow ripples, real folds show only at the turn-back and the hanging sides), its olive-yellow is even and the quilting is a regular diamond bump; the pillow is plump but smooth, without a sewn seam bead; tick stripes are printed-looking; the underside chart of the blanket bakes partly wrong where it lies on the tick (hidden in game). One 2048 set for a 2.5 m prop: soft at 1 m.
SM_Bed_Oak_PR.dresses: oak bed 2.5 x 1.36 x 1.15 m (head at -X): four capped posts, plank head and foot boards, pegged side rails, slats, a lumpy sagging straw tick in striped linen, a pressure-simulated pillow, a quilted wool blanket (olive-yellow, madder lining and border) simulated over the tick, hanging over the rails and turned back at the head end

SM_Chest_Small_PR.known_weaknesses: Round 2 unique bake, two review rounds (r6). Last look still faults: the red stain is rather even from board to board (edge wear to pale oak is there but slight), lid staves are hard to tell apart, the inside is stained like the outside instead of raw wood, rivets and the keyhole are baked not modelled, handles are plain bent rod.
SM_Chest_Small_PR.dresses: iron-bound chest 0.94 x 0.52 x 0.53 m, closed: red-stained plank carcase on two battens, coopered lid of seven staves between D-shaped ends, three forged straps riveted over lid and body with hinge knuckles at the back, eight corner irons, lock plate with keyhole and hasp, drop handles on eyes; real plank interior (see SM_Chest_Small_Open_PR)

SM_Gravestone_Round_PR.known_weaknesses: Stone reads as real rock (FieldBoulder scans) with moss and lichen in vertex colour; faults: the cross is two applied bars, no inscription, edges are pinched thin rather than chipped, the turfed mound is a smooth dome with a clean rim against the ground.

SM_Gravestone_Broken_PR.known_weaknesses: As the round stone; the fallen head does not match the break line of the stump; the skull beside it is the simple SM_Skull_PR. 4 material slots (limit 3).

SM_Skull_PR.known_weaknesses: Round 2 unique bake from a sculpt (ellipsoid union minus cavities, voxel remesh; cached), four review rounds (r6). NOT photoreal. Last look still faults: the brain case is too large for the face (the face is about a third of the height, so it reads slightly juvenile or stylised), surfaces are smooth and clay-like between features, the zygomatic arch is a straight rod, the mastoids are knobs, orbits and nasal aperture are shallow and not dark enough inside, the teeth are separate pegs without sockets, soil staining is patchy but mild; the squamous and other minor sutures are missing. Sutures (sagittal, coronal, lambdoid), pitting, hairline cracks, lichen specks and three lost teeth are there.
SM_Skull_PR.dresses: human skull without the jaw, 0.16 x 0.2 x 0.2 m, facing -Y, resting on its teeth and skull base: domed cranium with zig-zag sutures, brow ridges, orbits, pear-shaped nasal aperture, cheek bones and zygomatic arches, temporal fossae, palate, eleven upper teeth (three lost); stained and pitted old bone

SM_Bones_Scatter_PR.known_weaknesses: Round 2 unique bake, two review rounds (r6). Reads as human remains at the gameplay camera; at 1 m: the skull has the faults of SM_Skull_PR, long bones are near-straight shafts with ball knuckles (no real femur neck, tibial crest or fibula), ribs are plain curved flat rods, there is no spine, pelvis or hand bones, and no cloth or sinew; staining is mild.
SM_Bones_Scatter_PR.dresses: scatter of human remains, 0.8 x 0.7 m: a skull on its side, four long bones with knuckled spongy ends, five ribs (one short, snapped)

SM_Candle_Iron_PR.known_weaknesses: Same mesh and bake as SM_Prop_Candle_Holder_01 (textures T_Prop_Candle_Holder_01_* in Props/Prop_Candle_Holder_01); see there.

SM_Fireplace_Fieldstone_PR.known_weaknesses: Masonry reads as real rubble with dressed jamb stones; soot on fireback and breast is the vertex-colour soot switch on a coarse grid, so its edge is soft; logs are swept tubes with a charred middle, no bark, no split faces, no embers; the bressummer has no adze marks; stack top is cut square at 4.14 m as the mesh it replaces. Brick version of sprite 64 frame 5 not built.

SM_Basket_Wicker_PR.known_weaknesses: Weave is modelled as alternating bumps, one per stake: reads as wicker at gameplay distance, as a ribbed bowl at 1 m (no separate strands, no ends). Straw scan stands in for willow. Empty.

SM_Pie_Rustic_PR.known_weaknesses: NOT photoreal: crust is a tinted plaster scan on a lathe with crimps; no flake, no glaze, no filling showing. Reads as a pie at gameplay distance only.

SM_Potion_Flask_PR.known_weaknesses: NOT photoreal: the contract has no translucent material, so the flask is opaque dark glossy glass in one piece with a wood-coloured cork; no liquid level, no refraction.

SM_Counter_Oak_PR.known_weaknesses: Plain plank counter, believable but new-looking: no wear on the customer edge beyond vertex colour, dark box behind the open front instead of real shelves with goods.

SM_Post_Support_Oak_PR.known_weaknesses: One review round. Post and braces are clean sawn timbers with pegs; brace ends are butted, not housed; the stone pad is four dressed blocks.

SM_Cabinet_Oak_PR.known_weaknesses: One review round. A plain side table with deep aprons; the class name says cabinet but the sprite shows no doors or drawers, and none are modelled.

SM_Dungeon_Pillar_Twin_PR.known_weaknesses: One review round. Drums are lathes of the FieldBoulder scan: joints are thin gaps without mortar or chipping, mouldings are simple; the scan wraps round each drum with a seam.

SM_Rubble_Pile_PR.known_weaknesses: One review round. Blocks and stones are scattered by rule, some float a centimetre or intersect; the dust mound has a clean rim; no small debris.

SM_Shelf_Bottles_PR.known_weaknesses: One review round. Bottles are opaque glazed lathes of three shapes in three colours (sprite also has purple and teal), ten sides each, all upright and evenly spaced; the sprite's bottles are glass. Plank work is plain.

SM_Chest_Small_Open_PR.known_weaknesses: As SM_Chest_Small_PR (same bake). The interior is empty and stained like the outside; the lid is fixed at 102 degrees (no animation, swap meshes).

not_done: Round 2 did not reach, in the coordinator's order: fireplace (no soot bake, ash bed, firedogs or ember mask), gravestones, pie, basket, sign posts and doors (Structures/Misc untouched), and of the not-reached list everything except the two decals: beach shells / starfish / conch (Terrain/Scatter not taken over), fruit tree, hand tools, snake pillar, idol, fountain, free-standing arch, gold piles and coins, food, bookcase and empty shelf, hearts and pickups, shop sign, farm tools. No broken barrel states. Nothing imported into Unreal by this agent; the baked props need new materials per integration.contract.round2_material_upgrades (same asset names, pivots and bounds within millimetres; slot names changed to one MI_<Asset> per baked prop, see integration.assets).

validator.result: 37 assets, 21 pass, 20 errors, 169 warnings. All 24 baked props pass except three PIVOT errors that are by design (SM_Prop_Torch_Wall_01 wall-mounted, SM_Prop_Lantern_Hanging_01 hung from its hook, SM_Chest_Small_Open_PR keeps the closed chest's pivot). The other 17 errors are on the 13 unbaked round-1 props: UV_OVERLAP (tiling UVs, by design), PIVOT on the three gravestones, SLOTS_OVER on SM_Gravestone_Broken_PR.
validator.warnings: baked props: TEXEL_DENSITY above target on small props (2048 or 1024 px on a small object), TRIS_OVER_TARGET by 12-20 triangles on SM_Skull_PR and the candle

baked_assets.status: round 2: unique bake, reviewed; not claimed photoreal where known_weaknesses lists faults
baked_assets.material_exception: unique bake (T_<Asset>_BC/_N/_ORM and _E where listed), private to this prop, not a row of ART_STANDARD.md section 2: the coordinator asked for sculpted or displaced high-detail sources baked to the game mesh with AO and curvature edge wear, true metal in ORM.B and emissive masks, which the shared tiling library cannot carry. Non-overlapping UV0; no vertex colour.
